stories.headline: ‘De-risk, not decouple’: Bessent says US-China must cooperate on AI risks
stories.deck: The United States and China plan to initiate a dialogue on superintelligence risks during an upcoming meeting. US Treasury Secretary Scott Bessent highlighted the importance of cooperation in managing artificial intelligence risks. The discussion aims to address shared technological challenges and ensure human oversight remains paramount. Trade agreements have also been outlined to strengthen…
stories.bodyText:
The United States and China must work together to manage the risks posed by advanced artificial intelligence while recognising that their competition for technological leadership will continue, 
US treasury
 secretary Scott Bessent said on Tuesday.
Bessent said the two countries should not underestimate their differences as they prepare to establish a new dialogue on “superintelligence” during US President Donald Trump’s meeting with Chinese President Xi Jinping in Shenzhen next week.
The meeting, scheduled on the sidelines of the November 18-19 Asia-Pacific Economic Cooperation (APEC) leaders’ summit, will be Trump’s third meeting with Xi this year. Bessent, who is due to travel to China for the talks, said Washington wanted to build a relationship with Beijing based on “balance and reciprocity”.
“As SI advances, so will the need to engage in new areas of risk management — and to demonstrate how two nations can reconcile the demands of competition with the responsibilities of leadership,” Bessent said in prepared remarks to the National Committee on US-China Relations in New York.
He added that the two sides should “harbour no illusions about the differences between the United States and China”, noting that their interests and approaches would not always align.
US and China plan dialogue on superintelligence risks
The proposed dialogue on superintelligence, or SI, is intended to help Washington and Beijing address shared risks and avoid misunderstandings between their respective systems, Bessent said.
The discussions are expected to cover the evaluation and testing of advanced AI models before their release, as well as measures to ensure that human judgement remains in control of the technology.
“We also expect to exchange best practices for evaluating and testing advanced models before their release, and for keeping human judgment firmly in command of this technology,” he said.
The two countries have also agreed to establish a direct communication channel to alert each other about serious incidents involving the technology.
Trump and Xi agreed on the AI alert system during their previous meeting at the White House in September. However, Trump had then expressed reluctance to introduce additional safeguards, saying he wanted to protect US leadership in the field, Reuters reported.
Bessent outlines trade initiatives ahead of Trump-Xi meeting
Bessent also referred to trade agreements reached during the two previous Trump-Xi meetings, including plans for a “Board of Trade” to determine reciprocal tariff reductions on $30 billion worth of non-sensitive goods in each direction.
China has also pledged to purchase US agricultural products, he said.
A proposed “Board of Investment” would provide a structured forum to discuss market access for American companies operating in China and offer greater predictability for Chinese businesses, Bessent added.
He acknowledged that the US trade deficit with China remained a point of friction but reiterated that Washington's objective was to reduce risks in the economic relationship rather than sever trade ties.
“The US objective is to ‘de-risk, not to decouple’ from trade with China,” he said.
Bessent invoked the first US trade voyage to China in 1784, when American merchants exchanged ginseng for Chinese tea, porcelain and silk, to underline the importance of maintaining areas of cooperation despite competing interests.
Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang faces shareholder lawsuit
Bessent did not refer in his remarks to the controversy surrounding Nvidia chief executive Jensen Huang, who is facing an internal investigation by the company's board over reports of an affair with Alice Huang, a businesswoman suspected by US intelligence services of having links to Chinese intelligence.
China's foreign ministry has dismissed the espionage allegations as “groundless” and “a smear”. Nvidia has said its board has no reason to believe that US national security or the company's secrets were compromised, while Jensen Huang has pledged to cooperate with the internal review.
The controversy has also prompted a shareholder lawsuit against Nvidia and its chief executive.
According to news agency AP, retail investor Mark Kistenmacher filed a complaint in a California court on Monday, accusing the company and Huang of misleading investors about the relationship and its potential implications for national security and Nvidia's business.
The complaint alleges that Nvidia failed to disclose Huang's relationship with Alice Huang and made misleading statements about its dealings with her company, Singapore-based Megaspeed International. The company had earlier said its compliance team had checked Megaspeed's activities and found no evidence of wrongdoing, AP reported.
The lawsuit seeks unspecified damages and a jury trial on behalf of investors who purchased Nvidia shares between October 9, 2025, and November 8, 2026.
Nvidia's independent directors said on Tuesday that they had appointed the New York-based law firm Wachtell, Lipton, Rosen & Katz to conduct a “thorough and independent investigation” into the matter. Joon H. Kim, a partner at the firm and a former acting US attorney for the Southern District of New York, will lead the inquiry.
Trump said on Monday that the FBI was investigating the affair. He also said Huang had told him that he had no idea the woman could be involved in espionage, adding that he did not think the Nvidia chief had reason to worry.
Nvidia shares fell 4.3% on Monday, wiping out around $190 billion in market value, and declined a further 5.5% by Tuesday's close.
Huang has acknowledged the affair and apologised to his wife, family and the company in an open letter published on Nvidia's website.
“I support the investigation and will cooperate fully. I love our country and our company. I am committed to protecting NVIDIA and supporting America’s national security,” he said.

stories.headline: Army jawan posted with President’s Bodyguard shot in U.P.; condition stable
stories.deck: Incident took place on Deepavali night in Baghpat; efforts on by three police teams to nab two accused who remain at large
stories.bodyText:
A man posted as Army jawan in the Rashtrapati Bhavan security was allegedly shot by two neighbours following an old rivalry in Uttar Pradesh’s Baghpat district on Deepavali night.
Saurabh Tomar (26), serving in the elite President’s Bodyguard (PBG) regiment, underwent surgery at a private hospital in Meerut and is said to be stable. The bullet struck Mr. Tomar just behind the ear, the police said. His brother also suffered serious head injuries after being attacked with a stick.
The police have registered a case at Ramala police station against two accused and formed three police teams to arrest them, who remained at large.
A resident of the village, Mr. Tomar was recruited in 2021 and is currently posted at the Rashtrapati Bhavan. He was visiting the village on leave to celebrate Deepavali. On Sunday night (November 8, 2026), he was bursting firecrackers outside his home along with his brothers Vineet and Mintu when an argument allegedly broke out with two villagers, Dheeraj and his brother Monu alias Praveen.
“On 08.11.2026 at 9:45 p.m., Ramala police station received information that in village Gopalpur Khadana, Monu alias Praveen and Dheeraj, residents of the same village, fired a shot which ricocheted off the wall and hit the plaintiff’s son Saurabh (serving in Rashtrapati Bhavan security), injuring him. Vineet was also hit on the head with a stick and injured,” a statement by the Baghpat police read.
The complaint was filed by the Mr. Tomar’s father Janak Raj. “On receiving the information, Ramala police station immediately registered an FIR. Saurabh is undergoing treatment in a Meerut hospital. Both are in normal condition. Based on the complaint of the plaintiff/father Janak Raj, a case has been registered at Ramala police station. Three police teams have been formed to arrest the accused, and efforts are being made by them to arrest them,” the statement added.
The President's Bodyguard is the oldest and senior-most cavalry regiment in the Indian Army, stationed at the Rashtrapati Bhavan in New Delhi.
With PTI inputs
Published - November 11, 2026 08:39 am IST

stories.headline: ‘Ramayana’ movie battle sequence triggers viral interest in Keralam’s Jatayu Earth Center
stories.deck: The spectacular depiction of Ravana-Jatayu war in Ramayana: Part 1 has sparked global interest, turning Chadayamangalam’s Jatayu Earth Center into a viral trending destination across social media and travel vlogs
stories.bodyText:
The high-altitude battle where Jatayu attempts to wrest Sita from Ravana’s soaring Pushpak Vimana serves as a visual centrepiece in director Nitesh Tiwari’s Ramayana: Part 1.
Jatayu sculpture: A myth comes alive
Spanning 200 feet across a giant rock hill in Chadayamangalam, the monumental structure crafted by Rajiv Anchal reigns as the world’s largest bird sculpture. Following the film’s release, public figures from Chief Minister V.D. Satheesan to a multitude of prominent content creators have amplified the landmark’s reach. Viral Instagram reels and YouTube memes comparing the film’s visual effects with the real-life sculpture have captivated millions. National and international travel vloggers are broadcasting the site’s cable car experience, panoramic sunset views, and impressive architecture, effectively transforming a regional cultural beacon into a global bucket-list attraction.
Unique phase
Despite the digital frenzy, ground management is navigating a unique transitional phase as bookings catch up with online interest. “Nearly 90% of the destination’s visitors traditionally originate from north India, with local footfall remaining relatively modest. While average daily attendance hovers around 2,500 and swells to 5,000 during peak seasons, immediate travel spikes following the release have been tempered by the necessity for long-term trip planning and high festival airfares. However, inquiry volumes have surged dramatically, signalling an impending wave of domestic and international arrivals as travel itineraries are finalised,” says Deepak Sunil, CEO, earth center.
The management also admits they were caught unprepared for the sheer scale of exposure. Strategic planning sessions are currently under way to scale up proactive crowd management systems, address infrastructure gaps, and establish dedicated facilities to handle peak visitor flows seamlessly.
Beyond the immediate hilltop experience, the viral interest is creating substantial economic momentum for regional tourism ecosystem, boosting local hotels, resorts, transport providers, and tour guides. With travellers from neighbouring States and beyond increasingly incorporating Chadayamangalam into their itineraries, the small village also stands to gain from the site’s footprint on the global travel map. “The local body is fully prepared to provide all necessary tourist amenities. We plan to hold discussions with the management of the Jatayu Earth’s Center to address some key logistical issues, after which the panchayat will extend complete support to manage the visitor inflow during the upcoming season,” said Chadayamangalam panchayat president K. Sudevan.
Published - November 11, 2026 06:08 am IST

stories.headline: Jensen Huang backed nepotism in 2025 saying it doesn't bother him
stories.deck: Jensen Huang's recent revelation of his extramarital affair raises questions regarding Nvidia's leadership trajectory. During a company assembly, he passionately justified nepotism by highlighting the effectiveness of employee children within the firm. Notably, Huang's own offspring are in pivotal roles—Madison heads the Omniverse department, while Spencer concentrates on AI initiatives.
stories.bodyText:
Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang recently admitted to having an extramarital affair and soon after his admission, talks surrounding succession at Nvidia have gained momentum. Amid this, an older report has resurfaced in which Huang defended 
nepotism
 during a recent company all-hands meeting, claiming that employees' children often end up doing a better job than their parents. Speaking at a recent all-hands meeting last year, Huang acknowledged that many staff members’ children work at the company and insisted it doesn't bother him. He reasoned that parents wouldn't recommend their own kids for a job if they thought they would embarrass them – and added with a smile that many “Nvidia second-generation” employees even outperform their parents.
The comments come as Nvidia faces closer attention over its hiring practices, particularly because Huang’s own children, Madison and Spencer, have moved into key roles within the company’s emerging business divisions.
However, Nvidia has no public succession plan and no obvious heir. Huang holds both the CEO and president titles. Under him, Nvidia has taken an estimated 90% of the market for the chips behind large Al projects. According to a report, Huang has long rejected conventional hierarchy and once said on a podcast that traditional organisational charts made no sense to him. He runs Nvidia mostly through project meetings that bring together recent graduates and senior executives in the same room.
A rare family presence in Silicon Valley
Having multiple generations under one roof is unusual for Silicon Valley, where the children of tech pioneers like Apple's 
Steve Jobs
 and Microsoft’s Bill Gates typically steered clear of their parents' companies. At Nvidia, however, the family ties extend beyond the CEO. Children of co-founder Chris Malachowsky and Director Aarti Shah also work at the firm.
Rather than working in Nvidia’s core chip and data center business, Huang's children have carved out spots in newer, future-focused areas. Madison Huang leads the Omniverse department, focusing on 3D simulation and Digital Twin software. Spencer Huang concentrates on AI models and developing robotics perception software.
Madison’s rapid rise at Nvidia has drawn plenty of attention across the tech industry. Just four years after joining the company, she is part of her father's core leadership team, with a 2023 compensation package that topped $1 million. Spencer, meanwhile, has taken a quieter approach, working behind the scenes on Nvidia’s robotics goals while avoiding the spotlight.
Former Nvidia Vice President Greg Estes acknowledged the family connection, emphasising that both siblings “work very hard, excel in their respective fields, and have a deep attachment to the company.”

briefs.headline: Seven coaches of passenger train derail near Guwahati's Digaru railway station
Dozens injured in South Korea after bus crashes into 32 vehicles
briefs.deck: The bus collided with 32 vehicles before slamming into a median strip, fire officials said
briefs.bodyText:
A commuter bus struck more than 30 vehicles stopped at a traffic light during the morning rush hour on Wednesday (November 11, 2026) in Seongnam, just south of Seoul, injuring dozens of people, fire officials in South Korea said.
At least 57 people were being treated for injuries, including nine who were seriously hurt, although none were in life-threatening condition, according to the fire department of Gyeonggi Province, which governs Seongnam.
The bus collided with 32 vehicles before slamming into a median strip, fire officials said. Photos from the scene showed the bus perched on a median strip with a shattered windshield and other damaged cars.
Police were questioning the bus driver, who tested negative in a breathalyzer test and told investigators that the brakes had failed, according to Park Chang-gon, an official from Seongnam's Bundang district police station.

briefs.deck: Seven coaches, including the engine, of the Kolkata-Sairang Express derailed at Digaru railway station in Assam. The train was traveling from Sairang in Mizoram to Kolkata when the incident occurred. Several passengers sustained injuries, although no casualties have been reported so far. Senior railway officials have arrived at the accident site to assess the situation. The cause of the…
briefs.bodyText:
GUWAHATI: Seven coaches, including the engine, of the Kolkata-Sairang Express derailed near Digaru, on the outskirts of Guwahati, early Wednesday morning.
The train was travelling from Sairang in Mizoram to Kolkata when the accident occurred.
Several passengers were reportedly injured.
No casualties have been reported so far.
Kapinjal Kishore Sharma, chief public relations officer (CPRO) of Northeast Frontier Railway, told news agency ANI that senior railway officials had rushed to the spot following the incident.
The cause of the derailment is not yet known.

briefs.headline: Ukraine’s Zelenskyy says he is pleased with messages from U.S. envoys on diplomatic efforts to end war
briefs.deck: “I see changes. I am very happy about what I hear,” Mr. Zelenskyy said when asked about the recent messages by U.S. presidential ‌envoys ⁠Jared Kushner and Steve Witkoff
briefs.bodyText:
Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelenskyy said on Tuesday (November 10, 2026) he was very happy with messages he was getting from the U.S. in terms of moving towards a resolution of the more than four-and-a-half-year-old war with Russia.
Mr. Zelenskyy was addressing journalists after a day of talks with Nordic leaders in Denmark, as a first day of U.S.-led trilateral discussions between Ukraine, Russia and the U.S. wrapped up in Abu Dhabi.
“I see changes. I am very happy about what I hear,” Mr. Zelenskyy said when asked about the recent messages by U.S. presidential envoys Jared Kushner and Steve Witkoff.
Mr. Zelenskyy has been careful to smooth over what has often been a volatile relationship with U.S. President Donald Trump, particularly after a February 2025 Oval Office meeting during which Mr. Trump accused him of being ungrateful.
The talks in Abu Dhabi are the first three-sided discussions to be held since February. Mr. Zelenskyy described the first day as constructive and substantive.
Later, in his latest comments to journalists, Mr. Zelenskyy said the agenda of the talks in Abu Dhabi had included formulating a new security architecture for Europe, an idea raised earlier on Tuesday (November 10, 2026) by Russian Foreign Minister Sergei Lavrov.
Mr. Zelenskyy said the notion was “very difficult”.
“We are all very cautious with this topic because nobody really understands 100% what they want. I think we understand, but nobody saw the documents, what the Americans discussed with the Russians,” Mr. Zelenskyy said.
He said the idea was first raised by Russian President Vladimir Putin in 2021 and the administration of President Joe Biden at the time was cautious about it as the sequence of what had to be done first was important.
“Everybody is ready for dialogue. First, stop the war in Ukraine. Second, security guarantees for Ukraine. Third, maybe some dialogue about the topic of security in Europe, in the world,” Mr. Zelenskyy said.
“This sequence is very, very important in this case.”
Earlier, Mr. Lavrov had said Moscow would not agree to an immediate ceasefire without knowing what would happen next.
He said it would be wiser to discuss the outlines of the future security architecture in Europe first, and then a ceasefire in Ukraine.

briefs.headline: No talks underway with U.S., says Iran top security official
briefs.deck: Iran ‌has insisted ‌the ⁠U.S. must meet ⁠seven conditions set out in a June interim agreement ​before the ‌Strait of Hormuz can reopen and negotiations resume
briefs.bodyText:
Iran’s top security official Mohsen Rezaei said there are currently no negotiations taking place between Tehran and Washington, in an interview with pro-Iran broadcaster Al-Mayadeen.
Iran has insisted the U.S. must meet seven conditions set out in a June interim agreement before the Strait of Hormuz can reopen and negotiations resume.
Mr. Rezaei said Iran had asked the U.S. for a “clear and explicit” response to its conditions, but had yet to receive one, adding that Washington could respond in the future.
After meeting with mediator Qatar on Monday (November 9, 2026), U.S. President Donald Trump played down the likelihood of major warfare restarting soon but remained unwilling to accept the existing Iranian truce plan.

briefs.headline: U.S. Treasury chief Bessent moved to military base after Iranian threats, reports say
briefs.deck: Iran has previously denied plotting to attack ‌officials and people on U.S. soil
briefs.bodyText:
U.S. Treasury Secretary Scott Bessent recently moved out of his home and onto a military base after Iranian threats against his life, the New York Times reported on Tuesday (November 10, 2026), citing sources with knowledge of the matter.
Iran has ramped up efforts to target U.S. personnel, and lethal plots by Tehran against American citizens have reached “advanced stages”, a senior intelligence official in the Trump administration warned in a memo seen by Reuters late last month.
The newspaper reported that the severity of the threats to Mr. Bessent was not immediately clear.
Iran has previously denied plotting to attack officials and people on U.S. soil.
The newspaper reported that U.S. officials have noted that Iran’s ability to carry out large-scale attacks in the US and other territories overseas is limited.
The U.S. Treasury Department did not immediately respond to a request for comment.
Mr. Bessent has been the face of Washington’s economic pressure campaign against Tehran during the course of the U.S.-Israeli war on Iran that began on February 28.
U.S.-Israeli strikes on Iran and Israeli attacks on Lebanon during the war have killed thousands and displaced millions. American and Israeli attacks have also killed top Iranian officials, including the late Supreme Leader Ayatollah Ali Khamenei.
Published - November 11, 2026 06:47 am IST

briefs.headline: Trump ally Jim Jordan elected U.S. House Republican leader after midterm election rout
briefs.deck: The Ohio Congressman will replace House Speaker Mike Johnson, who announced he was stepping down from leadership after Republicans lost control of both chambers of Congress
briefs.bodyText:
Jim Jordan, a hardline ally of President Donald Trump, was elected leader of the Republicans in the U.S. House of Representatives on Tuesday (November 10, 2026), defeating fellow conservative Steve Scalise as the party reckons with a crushing midterm election defeat.
Mr. Jordan, the combative chairman of the House Judiciary Committee, beat the current majority leader by 106 votes to 73 in a secret ballot, U.S. media reported, putting him in charge of the party's opposition to the incoming Democratic majority.
The Ohio congressman will replace House Speaker Mike Johnson, who announced he was stepping down from leadership after Republicans lost control of both chambers of Congress in last week's elections.
Senate Republicans meanwhile reelected John Thune as their leader, retaining their existing leadership team despite demands from conservatives for a reckoning over the election losses.
Mr. Jordan, a founding member of the hard-right House Freedom Caucus, had pitched himself as the fighter Republicans need to confront Democrats during the final two years of Trump's presidency.
His victory represented a rejection of the party's established leadership, with Mr. Scalise having served in senior Republican positions for more than a decade.
Both men are staunch Trump allies, but the president declined to endorse either candidate.
The contest was a rematch of their 2023 battle for the speakership following the ouster of Kevin McCarthy.
Mr. Scalise initially won the Republican nomination but withdrew after failing to secure sufficient support, while Mr. Jordan subsequently lost three votes on the House floor before Mr. Johnson emerged as a compromise candidate.
Mr. Jordan, a former champion wrestler who has represented Ohio in Congress since 2007, built his reputation as a political brawler and fierce critic of the Republican establishment. Former speaker John Boehner once branded him a "legislative terrorist" for his uncompromising tactics.
He also emerged as a leading defender of Mr. Trump during congressional investigations into the president's attempts to overturn his 2020 election defeat.
Mr. Thune's reelection as Senate Republican leader came after conservative lawmakers temporarily stalled proceedings, demanding a clearer strategy for confronting the incoming Democratic majority. "I appreciated the opportunity to have an open, honest, and transparent conversation with my colleagues today," he said in a statement, adding that he was honored to retain their support.
Mr. Thune, who will become Senate minority leader in January, pledged to work with Mr. Trump and oppose Democratic efforts to enact what he called their "far-left, liberal agenda."
Published - November 11, 2026 06:54 am IST

briefs.headline: U.S. and China should stay clear-eyed on AI cooperation and competition, says Scott Bessent
briefs.deck: Bessent, who will travel to China next week for U.S. President Donald Trump’s third meeting this year with Chinese President Xi Jinping, said that he wanted to “build a constructive relationship on the basis of balance and reciprocity”
briefs.bodyText:
The United States and China should harbor no illusions about their differences on artificial intelligence as they navigate cooperation to mitigate the technology’s risks while competing for Artificial Intelligence (AI) supremacy, U.S. Treasury Secretary Scott Bessent said on Tuesday (November 10, 2026).
Mr. Bessent, who will travel to China next week for U.S. President Donald Trump’s third meeting this year with Chinese President Xi Jinping, said in prepared remarks to the National Committee on U.S.-China Relations in New York that he wanted to “build a constructive relationship on the basis of balance and reciprocity.”
The meeting in Shenzhen, to be held on the sidelines of the November 18-19 Asia-Pacific Economic Cooperation leaders summit, will advance a new bilateral dialogue on “superintelligence”, or SI, Bessent said, using the Trump administration’s preferred term for the technology.
The dialogue is meant to guard against shared risks and “prevent a misunderstanding between our two systems,” Bessent said.
“We also expect to exchange best practices for evaluating and testing advanced models before their release, and for keeping human judgment firmly in command of this technology,” he said, adding the two sides had agreed to establish a direct channel for alerting each other to serious incidents.
Mr. Trump and /Mr. Xi agreed on the new AI alert system during their previous meeting at the White House in September, but Trump at the time also said he was reluctant to add new guardrails because he wanted to preserve US leadership.
“As SI advances, so will the need to engage in new areas of risk management — and to demonstrate how two nations can reconcile the demands of competition with the responsibilities of leadership,” Mr. Bessent said.
“As we do so, we should harbor no illusions about the differences between the United States and China. As I stated earlier, our interests will not always coincide. And our approach to every challenge, likewise, will not always converge,” he added.
Nvidia questions
Mr. Bessent’s remarks made no mention of the controversy surrounding Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang, who is facing an investigation by the AI chipmaker’s board after a New York Times report that he had an affair with a businesswoman suspected by U.S. security services of being a Chinese intelligence asset.
China’s Foreign Ministry has called the spying accusations “groundless” and “a smear.”
Nvidia has said its board has no reason to believe U.S. national security or company secrets were compromised and that Huang has committed to cooperating with the internal review. Huang has told employees he was unfaithful to his wife, but provided no details about the relationship.
While Mr. Huang was present at the Trump-Xi summits in Beijing in May and in Washington in September, it was unclear if Trump would bring him to the APEC summit.
A fourth Trump-Xi summit this year is expected in December at the U.S.-hosted G20 summit in Miami.
Tariff cuts, trade deficit
In remarks that referred to the initial U.S. trade voyage to China in 1784 to trade American ginseng for Chinese tea, porcelain and silk, Bessent said that the U.S.-China relationship would be sustained by “the wisdom — and the will — to recognize where common purpose must prevail over competing interests.”
Bessent referred to other trade initiatives agreed during the two previous Trump-Xi summits, including the establishment of a “Board of Trade” to determine mutual tariff cuts on $30 billion of non-sensitive goods in each direction, and China’s pledged purchases of US farm goods.
A similarly structured “Board of Investment” will provide a structured forum for issues including market access for American companies in China and “increased predictability for Chinese companies,” he said.
He reiterated that the US trade deficit with China remains a source of friction, but the US objective is to “de-risk, not to decouple” from trade with China.

stories.headline: Passenger jumps onto track at Vijayanagar Metro station; Purple Line services briefly disrupted
stories.deck: According to the Bangalore Metro Rail Corporation Limited (BMRCL), the incident occurred at approximately 1.31 p.m.
stories.bodyText:
Bengaluru Metro services on the Purple Line were briefly disrupted on Tuesday (November 10, 2026) after a passenger jumped onto the track at Vijayanagar Metro Station while a train was approaching the platform.
According to the Bangalore Metro Rail Corporation Limited (BMRCL), the incident occurred at approximately 1.31 p.m. Station authorities immediately initiated emergency protocols, rescued the individual and shifted the passenger to a nearby hospital for medical treatment.
To facilitate rescue and safety operations while minimising inconvenience to commuters, BMRCL operated truncated services on two unaffected sections of the Purple Line — between Kempegowda (Majestic) and Whitefield (Kadugodi), and between Mysore Road and Challaghatta, according to a release.
Normal train operations on the Purple Line resumed from 1.58 p.m., around 27 minutes after the incident. BMRCL clarified that services on the Green Line and Yellow Line remained unaffected throughout the incident.

stories.headline: Policy to promote growth of civil aviation in Karnataka to be placed before next meeting of State Cabinet for clearance
stories.deck: Industries and Infrastructure Development Minister M.B. Patil said the suspension of flight services from Shivamogga Airport is due to shortcomings in the Union Government’s UDAN-2 policy.
stories.bodyText:
Industries and Infrastructure Development Minister M.B. Patil on Tuesday (November 10, 2026) announced that a comprehensive policy to promote the growth of civil aviation in Karnataka will be placed before the next meeting of State Cabinet for its clearance.
The Minister told media persons here that the policy covers several aspects, including financial assistance, Viability Gap Funding (VGF) and efficient management of airports operated by the State Government. The policy could serve as a model for the entire country, he added.
Shivamogga flight service suspension
He said the suspension of flight services from Shivamogga Airport is due to shortcomings in the Union Government’s UDAN-2 policy. “The Centre handed over Mangaluru Airport to the Adani Group and is now moving towards privatising Hubballi Airport. The State spent ₹1,000 crore on developing the Kalaburagi Airport and handed it over to the Centre, but has not received even a single rupee in return. Shivamogga MP B. Y. Raghavendra, who has been criticising the State Government, should take note of these facts,” Mr. Patil said.
“We had suggested extending the UDAN scheme from three years to five years, followed by another five years of joint operation by the State and Union Governments, with both sharing the expenditure equally. This would have yielded better results. However, the Centre did not give due consideration to our proposal. Consequently, flight operations at 17 airports across the country have now been suspended,” he said.
“It is not appropriate for the State to invest thousands of crores of rupees in building airports only to hand them over to the Union Government. That is why we are managing the airports at Shivamogga, Raichur and Vijayapura ourselves. Flight services at the previously non-operational Kalaburagi Airport were restored with 80 per cent of the funding provided by the Kalyana Karnataka Region Development Board (KKRDB) and the remaining 20 per cent by the State Government. If Raghavendra is capable, let him arrange similar funding for Shivamogga Airport,” Mr. Patil challenged.
Published - November 10, 2026 07:04 pm IST

stories.headline: ‘Heavens would not have come down to earth’: Karnataka high court questions haste in cutting 300 pomegranate plants
stories.deck: The Karnataka high court intervened after government officials in Kolar cut down over 300 pomegranate plants. The actions were taken without prior notice during the Diwali holidays, which raised concerns. The petitioner had submitted an application for land cultivation regularization, which was still under consideration. Justice KV Aravind questioned the urgency of the officials’ actions and…
stories.bodyText:
BENGALURU: The Karnataka high court has barred government officials in Kolar from entering a disputed agricultural property or taking further action there after the local tahsildar allegedly cut down more than 300 pomegranate plants.
Hearing an urgent petition on Monday during the Diwali vacation, Justice KV Aravind questioned the haste with which the authorities had acted. He observed that if the action had been delayed, "heavens would not have come down to the earth".
The petition was filed by TN Monica, a resident of Tippenahalli in Kolar taluk. The land in question falls within the limits of the Vemagal-Kurugal town panchayat.
The petitioner claimed that the tahsildar, accompanied by police personnel and other officials, entered the property around 3pm on November 7 and cut down more than 300 pomegranate plants without prior notice.
The court was informed that an application seeking regularisation of the cultivation on the land had been filed in 2023 and was still under consideration.
The petitioner further alleged that officials carried out the action during consecutive government holidays around Deepavali, despite requests to defer it until after her marriage, scheduled for November 15 and 16.
Justice Aravind questioned why the authorities had acted in such haste and whether postponing the operation from November 7 to another working day would have caused any immediate harm.
Pending further orders, the court directed the government not to take any action concerning the disputed property and barred officials from entering the land. It also issued notice to the state government and the district administration.
The next hearing is scheduled for Friday.

stories.headline: No family gathering? Singles find their own spark this Deepavali
stories.deck: Singles in Bengaluru are creating new traditions during the festive season, focusing on personal and meaningful celebrations. Communities like Singles Social and Phoenix Family provide opportunities for connection and support among single individuals and parents. Participants engage in festive gatherings, helping to alleviate feelings of loneliness and strengthen bonds. Many singles embrace…
stories.bodyText:
BENGALURU: Festivals are often imagined as occasions for family reunions, elaborate meals, and crowded homes. But for those living away from family, navigating separation or building independent lives, celebrations can also bring a sense of absence.
Social media, filled with photographs of family gatherings and festive get-togethers, can make that feeling more pronounced.
Yet being single does not necessarily mean spending the festive season alone. Across Bengaluru, individuals are finding new ways to experience festivals — through communities that offer companionship and a sense of belonging, friendships that become chosen families, and personal rituals that make celebrating alone equally meaningful.
Finding a festival family
Seeking to foster connections and ease festive-season loneliness, Singles Social, a community for singles and those seeking companionship, is hosting a Deepavali celebration in Bengaluru on Nov 14.
Founder Harsh Vardhan Arya said the event will feature festive lights, food, and an opportunity for members to connect. People who are single, separated, or have lost spouses can take part in the celebration.
"Singles Social seeks to create meaningful human connections in a world increasingly shaped by swipes and algorithms," said Arya, adding the community has a dedicated chapter for single parents.
The community does not charge a membership fee[cite: 1]. Participants share the cost of individual events. "If the hotel charges Rs 2,500 per person, members will pay the same amount," said Arya.
The community currently has about 2,500 members across India, including more than 700 in Bengaluru.
"Our gatherings are intended to provide a comfortable, non-judgmental setting, without the expectations associated with dating platforms, and offer members an extended support network, like a family," said Arya, adding, "We also provide women with a space where being single is not seen as being available.
After late gatherings, members accompany women travelling alone or drop them home."
Phoenix Family, a support group for single parents, hosted a Deepavali party last week.
"Festivals like Deepavali are all about warmth and belonging. We offer a safe, welcoming space — especially for single mothers — to simply relax and feel part of a family again," said Vignesh Balan, founder.
Rather than formal gatherings, the community organises lively, child-inclusive celebrations, with games that bring parents and children together.
"The idea is to ensure our members don't just get through the holidays as singles, but genuinely celebrate them as a chosen family," said Balan.
Singles Club India, a community for people over 40, brings members together through festival gatherings and other social activities.
The community, whose members include divorced, separated, widowed and never-married people, has organised festival get-togethers for three years.
Co-admin Srobona Das, a single mother who co-parents a teenage daughter, recalled spending New Year's Eve alone while her daughter was in Mumbai. She said meeting even one friend or joining a larger gathering could help.
There is no membership or participation fee, although members cover their own costs when events are held at external venues.
Events have ranged from vineyard visits to Sunday breakfasts and nights out. They are generally organised around themes and include food, music, icebreakers, games, and alcohol for those who choose to drink.
Attendance is confirmed in advance before venues, decorations and small giveaways are arranged. Previous gifts included Deepavali cookies, candles, and cakes.
For Koramangala café-bookstore owner Susan Timothy, 45, the experience of becoming a single parent changed the way her family celebrates Christmas.
The gatherings are now quieter. She also invites her household staff, their children and other single women, bringing everyone together for meals, gifts, and time around the Christmas tree.
'Better together'
Joy of celebrating on your own
Alone, however, does not always mean lonely. For many singles, festivals have become more personal and intentional. The celebrations may be smaller, but they can be deeply meaningful.
Social media strategist Ishita Banerjee, 25, who hails from Dibrugarh in Assam, misses the familiar chaos of celebrating at home. However, she has come to enjoy creating her own traditions and finding comfort in quieter celebrations.
Film director, screenwriter and lyricist Kavita Lankesh, a single parent, celebrates Deepavali with her daughter Esha and their pet dog, lighting a few diyas at home.
Being single has not diminished Saleela Kappan's festive celebrations. Living alone in Bengaluru, she remains closely connected to her family, friends, and neighbours.
She decorates her apartment with lights, particularly during Deepavali, and spends time with her six cats[cite: 1]. When alone, she enjoys cooking a special meal, decorating her home or travelling.
Hareeni Shetty, a single woman who works as a software engineer, lights one diya after finishing a late shift[cite: 1]. Shetty also cooks a festive meal using a family recipe while video-calling home.
Her mother, an elderly widow, decorates her doorway every year, not for guests but because the ritual continues to give the day meaning.
For some, the festive season means a crowded home and a table full of guests[cite: 1]. For others, it may be a meal with friends, a video call with family, a diya lit after work or simply an evening spent in their own company.
As Bengaluru's singles discover, the meaning of celebration does not have to depend on relationship status or the size of the gathering.

briefs.headline: Karnataka government moves contempt petition against Jenu Kuruba families in Nagarahole; they decry move and call it ‘high-handedness’
briefs.deck: The petition alleges that the tribal families have set up encampments inside the Nalkeri reserve forest in violation of an interim High Court court order. Families claim that they only built makeshift tarpaulin tents ahead of torrential rains.
briefs.bodyText:
The Karnataka government has moved a Contempt of Court petition at the Karnataka High Court against 39 Jenu Kuruba families in Nagarahole, accusing them of violating an interim order issued by the High Court in 2025.
The petition filed by Chief Secretary Shalini Rajaneesh and other government officials alleges that the tribal families have set up encampments inside the Nalkeri reserve forest, which forms part of the core/critical tiger habitat of Nagarahole Tiger Reserve, and claims this is in violation of the court order.
‘Six new tents’
Following a writ petition filed by one J.R. Ravi and others seeking urgent intervention ‘against the rejection of their individual forest rights claims under the Forest Rights Act (2006) and the continued attempts to dispossess them from their ancestral place, Karadikallu Atturu Kolli haadi (forest village), located in the Nagarahole Forest’, the High Court had issued an interim order of status quo in July 2025.
The order directed the petitioners not to put up any permanent structures and instructed both the petitioners and the government to maintain status quo as of the order date.
According to the government's claims, the community members built six new encampments in May 2026. The petition also accuses them of attempting to grab valuable government property and disturbing ecological balance by destroying vegetation and cutting trees inside the Reserved Forest.
‘Only makeshift tents for protection from rains’
The Nagarhole Adivasi Jamma Paale Hakku Sthapana Samithi has decried the government’s move, terming it a ‘perversion of justice’ and ‘bureaucratic highhandedness.’
Highlighting that the 39 families accused by the government of contempt of court are from Particularly Vulnerable Tribal Groups (PVTG) in Karnataka, the Samiti claimed that they have been following a strictly Constitutional Path to claim and safeguard their rights.
“Since May 5, 2025, the families of Karadikallu have been living together in a communal setting on their ancestral land because of this status quo order on July 18, 2025, albeit stripped of their basic right to shelter, life and fundamental human rights,” a statement from the organisation said.
According to them, in May 2026, ahead of the monsoons, which bring torrential rains to the Kodagu region, the families reworked their temporary shelters in which they had been staying.
“These are makeshift tarpaulin tents, solely to protect infants, elderly members and women from the harsh monsoon rains of Kodagu,” the statement said.
The photos submitted by the government as part of the petition also show structures that seem like temporary tents.
“Yet, in a display of utter malice and hostility, the Congress administration and its State Forest Department have chosen to interpret this survival measure as a violation of status quo,” the Samiti said.
The matter is listed for a hearing on November 19.
Rights vs conservation
According to tribal community members in the region, families who inhabited the forest were forced out by the Forest Department into nearby coffee plantations to work as daily wage labourers, in 1983-84.
On May 5, 2025, several tribal families re-entered the forest, claiming that they had been waiting for years for the Government to approve their claims under FRA. This resulted in tensions between the community and the Forest Department officials. In the same year, the community members filed a writ petition with the Karnataka High Court.

briefs.headline: Students present solutions to tackle food waste, nutrition and climate change at STHIRA 2026
briefs.deck: STHIRA 2026 in Bengaluru gives a platform for innovations supporting sustainable food. The finale held at BIC Bengaluru decided the three final winners
briefs.bodyText:
The third edition of STHIRA 2026, a sustainable food innovation challenge, was jointly hosted by Foodwize and the University of Gastronomic Sciences of Pollenzo, Italy recently at BIC Bengaluru. The competition saw participants from over 80+ teams from across 16 States in India under various disciplines of education, from chefs and engineers to humanities students.
The finale of STHIRA 2026 brought together 11 finalist teams from universities across India. The participating teams exhibited their prototypes and presented their innovations within the given time limit. The five-member jury evaluated the teams based on various factors including nutrition, cultural influence and climate resilience.
The four themes for this edition are access to nutrition, better livelihoods for small scale farmers, shaping urban food futures and reviving indigenous ingredients and traditional practices.
Incorporated in 2023 by Srijata Sengupta and Priya Joshi, Foodwize is a social initiative focusing on food systems, food cultures, transformation, development and experience design. Talking about the finale, Srijata says, “The purpose behind STHIRA was to encourage students to find solutions for some of the complex problems in our food systems today.”
The three winning teams receive a cash prize. “The winners will also receive hand-painted plates as trophies. We’ve been following this design so that our trophy is not just another cup but something deeply rooted with food and culinary traditions,” says Priya.
The presented prototypes included food solutions for artificial food colouring, exhibited as a solution through extracted natural pigmentation from beetroots and dragon fruit peels. A prototype focused on gut health and fighting heat through a traditional Odisha drink, Tanka Torani traditionally prepared as an offering for Lord Jagannath.
Further innovative ideas included nutritious food choices for present day college students who skip breakfast. A reintroduction of the traditional podi used to enhance tastes of various dishes or consumed with southern Indian breakfast staples including idli and dosa.
Abria Koshy, a student from IHM Aurangabad says, “STHIRA gave us an opportunity to come up with sustainable idea for present-day food challenges. My team, Rasa Roots focuses on making condiments through regional ingredients from Kerala and Mizoram.”
STHIRA and Foodwize also present multiple opportunities to all the finalist participants in taking their innovation forward. Their MOU with IIM Bengaluru helps the participants get an opportunity to enter the NSRCEL startup incubator programme.
“We are starting this incubator program to nurture food enterprises that are committed to sustainable food products and services,” says Priya “They also focus on the livelihoods of people in the supply chain, on the environmental impact of their business and their contribution to protecting and preserving food cultures.” The incubator is designed to provide six months of mentoring capability development and nurturing support.
One of the winning teams, Waste to Wax by Saranya Warrier of Amrita Vishwa Vidyapeetaam, focused on converting jackfruit processing residues into natural coatings.
Full Circle Feed Co. by Anushka Sahu, Antman Deshpande, Aditya Kannojia of IIM, Indore, also a winning entry, addresses organic food waste and rising animal feed costs by converting market waste into locally produced feed.
Poshan Plate by Suhas Bhat, Sahana Shetty, Rohit Rawal of Alliance University, working to improve nutritional quality and dietary diversity in institutional meals was another winner.
Jury member, K L Mukesh says, “Initiatives like this will introduce more entrepreneurs in the ecosystem. Fresh start-ups and small businesses will create a lot of new employment opportunities with diversity.”

briefs.headline: Germany and Ireland emerge as preferred destinations for higher education for Indian students
briefs.deck: Out of more than 60,000 students who are going to Germany, 12,000 students (20%), are from Karnataka, says Karan Lalit, Executive Director, South Asia, TOEFL and GRE
briefs.bodyText:
Even as Test of English as a Foreign Language Internet-Based Test (TOEFL iBT) is accepted in thousands of institutions around the world, Germany and Ireland are gaining prominence as higher education destinations among Indian students.
In an exclusive interview with The Hindu, Karan Lalit, Executive Director, South Asia, TOEFL and Graduate Record Examinations (GRE), said, “Most Indian students aspiring to study abroad have been opting for Germany and Ireland institutions in the past two years rather than the USA, the UK, Canada and Australia, that were traditionally chosen by many. This is what the data reveals.”
What numbers show
“According to Deutscher Akademischer Austauschdienst or German Academic Exchange Service (DAAD), which is the world’s largest funding organisation for international exchange of students in Germany, the number of Indian students enrolled in German universities reached 69,816 in the winter semester of 2025–26, marking a 17.5% year-on-year increase. Similarly, Ireland recorded approximately 9,175 Indian student enrolments in 2024–25, accounting for 20.6% of its non-Irish- domiciled student cohort,” he explained.
The TOEFL iBT test is accepted by institutions in both Germany and Ireland and is recognised by more than 13,500 institutions across over 160 countries worldwide, offering students greater flexibility to explore higher education opportunities across multiple destinations.
When asked about the number of students travelling to Germany from Karnataka, he said, “Out of more than 60,000 students who are going to Germany, 12,000 students – which is 20% – are from Karnataka.”
Return on investment
The reason why most students from Karnataka are choosing Germany and Ireland is not just VISA policies, but Return On Investment factor. “Now, most of the English tests are not accepted in Germany except TOEFL. Students are looking for ROI factor as they borrow loans from bank or their parents invest lakhs in higher education to study abroad. Additionally, Germany offers world-class engineering technology. There is an 18-month post-study work right that students get,” he explained.
He also noted that students, especially from Bengaluru, who have their own start-up ideas choose Germany. “Both Germany and Ireland work as apt destinations, especially when the US is not accepting a lot of students. Students who want to study healthcare or social sciences are choosing Ireland. The benefit is similar to Germany, with 18 months of work opportunity post graduation.”
While the comparable data on the university rejection rates for Indian students across the USA, the UK, Canada and Australia are not available in a consistent format, Mr. Lalit maintained that the university application outcomes depend on several factors, not just language assessments.
“These include academic performance, programme requirements and institutional selection criteria. Standardised assessments, advance planning and guidance from trusted overseas education counsellors can help students understand admission requirements, evaluate their options and prepare stronger applications. Visa decisions are a separate process and should not be conflated with university admission outcomes,” he said, adding, “Even if I want to go to the US, either there are no slots available or the VISA rejection rates have actually gone up.”
Gen-Z focussed questions
Karan Lalit highlighted how TOEFL underwent a lot of changes in January 2026, to make it more Gen-Z focused. “We want to make sure that TOEFL holds its credibility with the universities abroad. The duration of the test is 90 minutes now, down from 180 minutes earlier. The format of the test has changed, too. There are four skills required to succeed in TOEFL test which is reading, writing, listening and speaking. The questions framed are simpler, more Gen Z-focused and more adaptive in nature. So we call it Multi-Stage adaptive Test (MST).”
The result that was earlier released in 7 to 10 days, now takes only 72 hours. There are also 21 full-length mock tests comprising 3,000 practise questions offered to students at a nominal price of $5.

briefs.headline: PM Modi and Railway Minister likely to flag off Bengaluru–Mangaluru–Goa Vande Bharat Express on November 13

briefs.bodyText:

briefs.headline: Bengaluru’s The Counterpoint Crew presents Dakshin Diaries at Alliance Française de Bangalore
briefs.deck: A Cappella ensemble The Counterpoint Crew recently brought a multi-lingual musical experience to the stage with songs in various languages
briefs.bodyText:
The Counterpoint Crew recently performed Dakshin Diaries at Alliance Française de Bangalore. As a multilingual crew of 20 members, this Bengaluru-based music ensemble brought forward a curated list of classical melodies reimagined through the a cappella tradition.
Founded by Kavitha Ramesh last year, The Counterpoint Crew consists of around 25 members, most of whom are, “working professionals and also trained Hindustani and Western classical singers,” says Kavitha.
The songs they presented ranged from classical Italian and French compositions to vintage tunes set by Ilaiyaraaja and AR Rahman. The Crew reimagines popular fan-favourites from films and classical compositions and presents them in an all-immersive musical format. The speciality of a cappella performances is the absence of musical instruments.
The Crew was formed following Kavitha’s desire to join a choir in the city, and her inability to find one. “I also wanted to do something about the multilingual aspect of music — something that larger audiences would relate to.” Bengaluru being a cosmopolitan city made it easier to establish an ensemble.
She says, “We took relatable musical pieces and rearranged them in a choral fashion using the Western classical technique; that is how we are able to reach larger numbers.”
One of the songs performed at the event is an original composition by choir member Kaushik Mahalengam. Titled ‘Paravaye,’ and composed in Tamil, the song is about birds, the environment and mountains. “This is the first time we are performing the song live,” says Kaushik. The a cappella arrangement was prepared by Kavitha for this live performance.
The song came to Kaushik during a morning walk, about a year ago. “If you listen to the lyrics, it passes through different regions and talks about the birds in those places,” he says, adding this song echoes a person’s desire while looking at a bird soaring majestically. “I also want to be free like them; they don’t have any constraints. That is the inspiration behind ‘Paravaye’.”
Members of The Crew come from different States in India, making their performances and compositions diverse. The group came up slowly, with Kavitha reaching out to people she knew and the news spread through word of mouth. "If you ask any chorister, they know every single song, whether it is in Tamil, Hindi or Malayalam.”
The crew also performed ‘Maa’ from Taare Zameen Par (2007), ‘Botany’ from Shiva (1990) and ‘Kanmani Anbodu’ from Gunaa (1991) in both Telugu and Tamil. “The popularity of ‘Kanmani’ after Manjummel Boys made the song a perfect choice for this performance.” From ‘Ave Maria’ to ‘Seetha Kalyana Vaibhogame’, Dakshin Diaries travelled across global compositions before landing in Bengaluru for the finale, a Raghu Dixit composition in Kannada.

briefs.headline: Open letter raises objections to proposed reduction of lake, stormwater drain buffers across Karnataka
briefs.deck: The proposed reductions are driven by real estate interests, disregarding the CPHEEO’s technical guidelines on drainage planning and existing judicial directions on lakes, reads the letter
briefs.bodyText:
Mapping Malnad, a citizen-led platform for research, advocacy and dialogue to protect the Western Ghats, has written an open letter to the Urban Development Department, raising objections to the proposed reduction of lake and stormwater drain buffers across Karnataka.
“The proposed reductions are driven by real estate interests, disregarding the Central Public Health and Environmental Engineering Organisation’s (CPHEEO) technical guidelines on drainage planning and existing judicial directions on lakes,” said the letter, presenting eight grounds of objection.
Inadequate consultation
In a draft notification dated October 9, the Karnataka government proposed changes to the zoning rules across Karnataka (excluding regions under GBA, BDA, BMRDA and BMICAPA) to standardise buffer zones around water bodies such as lakes and drains.
Buffer zones for lakes
Buffer zones for drains
The letter pointed out that despite its far-reaching implications for Karnataka’s lakes, stormwater drains, water security and public safety, the draft notification was not publicised through prominent newspapers or readily accessible government websites, nor did it provide an email address for submitting objections.
Citing RTI documents, the letter noted that the move is driven by real estate interests.
“On 31.08.2024, in a meeting held under the chairmanship of the Honourable Deputy Chief Minister and Bengaluru Urban Development Minister to discuss the real estate sector in the Bengaluru Metropolitan Region, it was considered appropriate to carry out necessary activities in the buffer areas of nalas and water bodies, and accordingly, it was suggested to make appropriate amendments to the Karnataka Lake Conservation and Development Authority Act,” read a document detailing the proceedings of a meeting held under the chairmanship of the Chief Secretary, Government of Karnataka, on 10.07.2025.
The letter by Mapping Malnad pointed out that the lake buffer reductions were subsequently notified in February through amendments to the Karnataka Tank Conservation and Development Authority Act, 2014.
“The five corporations under the Greater Bengaluru Authority (GBA) have since unveiled plans for new roads and road widening, with alignments cutting across lakes, drains, their buffers and green spaces. These roads pave the way for unsustainable real estate development at the cost of Bengaluru’s defences against floods and water scarcity. We can expect the same to happen across Karnataka,” it noted.
Overlooking directions
While the CPHEEO’s Manual on Storm Water Drainage Systems, 2019 recommends comprehensive city drainage master plans aligned with city master plans, “these have not been prepared, as confirmed by our review of Approved Master Plans (AMPs) on the Department of Town and Country Planning (DTCP) website and enquiries with local planning offices,” the letter noted.
It also highlighted that the AMPs neither classify drains as primary, secondary or tertiary, nor demarcate their buffers, which could hinder the proper enforcement of buffer regulations.
In a judgment dated April 11, 2012, the Karnataka High Court accepted the Justice N.K. Patil Committee’s report, which not only considered the existing 30-metre lake buffer essential, but also recommended increasing it by 2 metres for every additional 5 hectares beyond 40 hectares of lake area, and called for rigorous enforcement of drain buffers in zonal regulations.
The letter noted that the reductions disregard these judicial directions. It also argues that the amendments undermine Karnataka’s water security, as the State is highly vulnerable to droughts, exacerbate the risk of floods, landslides, water pollution and public health hazards, and encourage encroachment.

briefs.headline: Out on bail in 1st case, Mangaluru priest now faces 2nd POCSO case involving 13-year-old boy
briefs.deck: In a troubling development, 65-year-old Father Cyprian Pinto, a Catholic priest, is now implicated in a second sexual assault case involving a minor. This new allegation was registered at the Mangaluru Women Police Station, concerning an incident from May 13, 2026. Earlier, a complaint regarding his inappropriate behavior towards a 14-year-old boy was filed on October 15.
briefs.bodyText:
MANGALURU: A 65-year-old Catholic priest in Mangaluru has been booked in a second case over allegations of sexually assaulting a minor boy, weeks after he was arrested in a separate case involving another teenager.
The latest complaint accuses Father Cyprian Pinto of sexually assaulting a 13-year-old boy in May this year, police said.
The case was registered at Mangaluru Women Police Station following a complaint alleging that the incident took place on May 13, 2026.
According to the complaint, the boy, a resident of Permannur village, regularly attended Sunday prayers at a church. The alleged assault took place when he was associated with the church, police said.
Police have registered a case under Section 75(2) (sexual harassment) of the Bharatiya Nyaya Sanhita (BNS) and Sections 8 and 12 of the Protection of Children from Sexual Offences (POCSO) Act.
Further investigation has been entrusted to the Assistant Commissioner of Police (ACP), Central Sub-Division.
Mangaluru City Police Commissioner Sudheer Kumar Reddy CH confirmed that the second complaint had been registered and said the ACP, Central Sub-Division, was conducting further investigation.
Earlier POCSO case against Father Cyprian Pinto
The latest complaint comes weeks after another case was registered against the same priest at Mangaluru South Police Station on October 15 over allegations of sexually harassing a 14-year-old boy.
In that case, Pinto was arrested and produced before a court on October 18. He was remanded to judicial custody until October 30 and was subsequently released on bail.
The investigation into the earlier case is still underway.
Police have not disclosed further details of the investigation in the latest case.
(With PTI inputs)

briefs.headline: Kautilya's Arthashastra gets Unesco recognition
briefs.deck: Kautilya's Arthashastra has been honored by UNESCO, earning a place on the MOWCAP Regional Register. A rare 16th-century manuscript stored at the Oriental Research Institute of the University of Mysore was digitized, revealing insights into governance, finance, and law. Rediscovered by Rudrapatnam Shamasastry in 1905 and later published in 1909, this recognition celebrates the institute's…
briefs.bodyText:
MYSURU: Kautilya's Arthashastra, an ancient treatise on governance and statecraft, has been inscribed on 
Unesco
's prestigious Memory of the World Committee for Asia and the Pacific (MOWCAP) Regional Register. An original 16th-century palm-leaf manuscript of the text, preserved and digitised by Oriental Research Institute (ORI) at University of Mysore, is among the institute's most prized collections.
Announcing the recognition, Unesco noted that the Indian manuscript outlines ancient statecraft, public finance and law. The manuscript has been included under the category 'Ancient Governance, History, and Modern Alignment', according to MOWCAP.
"It is a proud milestone in preserving and celebrating India's timeless intellectual heritage," ORI director D P Madhusudanacharya said.
Manuscript is digitised 
MOWCAP is a Unesco programme that identifies, preserves and promotes documentary heritage of outstanding historical, cultural and intellectual significance in Asia-Pacific region.
Madhusudanacharya said a team of experts from Indira Gandhi National Centre for the Arts, New Delhi, had visited the institute and reviewed the manuscript. 
"This recognition brings great honour to the institute, the University of Mysore and the entire Indian manuscript research community," he siad.
The manuscript was discovered at ORI in 1905 by scholar and librarian Rudrapatnam Shamasastry, who subsequently published the text in 1909.
The discovery brought the ancient Indian treatise back to scholarly attention. The manuscript has since been digitised as part of the institute's conservation efforts.

stories.headline: Crude cools off: Oil prices hold near $90 per barrel as US-Iran war tensions ease
stories.deck: Recent trends reveal that oil prices have settled around $90 per barrel, reflecting a decrease in tensions between the US and Iran. This cooling has alleviated concerns over possible supply shortages in the Middle East. Furthermore, President Trump has suggested that military intervention is not required at this point as diplomatic negotiations persist. However, challenges such as export…
stories.bodyText:
Oil prices remained around the $90-per-barrel mark, with Brent crude futures trading at $92.29 per barrel, up 80 cents or 0.87%, while US West Texas Intermediate (WTI) crude futures rose 57 cents or 0.66% to $86.61 per barrel.
Both benchmarks had settled at their lowest levels since August 31 for a second consecutive session.
The decline comes as easing tensions between the US and Iran have reduced concerns over prolonged supply disruptions in the Middle East.
Brent has shed around 17% in recent trading sessions, with Middle Eastern crude exports recovering to near pre-war levels. The recovery has also fuelled concerns about a potential supply glut, adding to the pressure on oil prices.
Earlier on Monday, US President Donald Trump said that war with Iran was "militarily ... effectively over", signalling that he was not immediately considering a return to large-scale attacks.
"We're just keeping it the status quo," Trump told reporters during an appearance at the White House after meeting Qatar's Prime Minister Sheikh Mohammed bin Abdulrahman bin Jassim Al Thani.
Trump said Iran had been "decapitated", but added that Washington was still seeking a long-term arrangement to ensure Tehran's nuclear programme was dismantled. 
Describing negotiations as showing "positive momentum", he said there was a "good chance" the conflict could end.
"They're talking to us, and they're talking very politely, And we'll see what happens," he said.
He added that military action did not currently appear necessary, although US forces remained prepared to resume operations if circumstances changed.
"The military action doesn't seem to be a very necessary thing, but we're locked and loaded, ready to go for any reason that changes," Trump said.
Trump also said the US would maintain its naval blockade in the Strait of Hormuz for now.
Meanwhile, Middle Eastern crude exports have recovered close to pre-war levels, while OPEC production increased in October, led by Saudi Arabia, Kuwait and Iraq, according to a Reuters survey. However, export constraints, depleted global inventories and disrupted fuel shipments continue to pose challenges. Industry leaders have warned that rebuilding oil stocks could take up to two years.

stories.headline: NMDC said to be in talks with Russia’s Rosatom over lithium investments
stories.deck: Rosatom and Russian miner Nornickel, however, are developing the country’s largest lithium deposit through their PolarLithium joint venture, with commercial production expected to begin by 2030
stories.bodyText:
Indian state-run miner NMDC Ltd. is in talks with Russia’s Rosatom to invest in Russian lithium projects, three people familiar with the matter said, as India steps up efforts to secure supplies of the metal for its battery and EV industries.
NMDC officials visited Russia last month for a conference and also held talks with state nuclear firm Rosatom, two of the people said.
The third person, who also confirmed that company officials had met with Rosatom, said NMDC was keen to explore lithium mining and processing opportunities in Russia and had also held discussions with other Russian companies.
All three people, who asked not to be named as the talks were confidential, said discussions between NMDC and Rosatom remain preliminary. A Rosatom spokesperson did not address Reuters queries about the meetings last month but said the Russian company was not currently engaged in talks with NMDC.
NMDC did not respond to a Reuters request for comment. NMDC said last year it was exploring acquisition opportunities for critical minerals in Africa, Australia and South America as part of its global mineral diversification strategy.
It has formed a 12-member team to carry out due diligence on potential critical mineral assets, one of the people said.
Last week, Indian Prime Minister Narendra Modi’s cabinet approved an incentive policy worth ₹28.14 billion ($297million) to boost domestic processing of lithium and nickel. India’s domestic processing capacity for critical minerals, including lithium, remains at a nascent stage, the government has said, leaving it heavily dependent on imports.
It currently meets lithium demand primarily through imports from China, Vietnam and Ecuador.
Despite possessing large lithium reserves, Russia currently has no commercial production. Rosatom and Russian miner Nornickel, however, are developing the country’s largest lithium deposit through their PolarLithium joint venture, with commercial production expected to begin by 2030.

stories.headline: Builder withheld Rs 88 lakh after redevelopment deal; landowners win over Rs 1.22 crore
stories.deck: The dispute originated in 2010, when two landowners, along with their late mother, transferred their development rights to a builder for redevelopment. They held a one-third undivided share in a property in Mumbai, and executed an Agreement to Assign for the redevelopment. Subsequently, they also entered into a Supplementary Agreement dated February 18, 2015, and an Agreement to Offer Permanent…
stories.bodyText:
You give your land for redevelopment to a builder but the latter does not honour his commitment fully, withholds the promised payments, and also fails to honour other contractual commitments when the flat is handed over to you. What options do you have then?
A recent ruling by the Maharashtra Consumer Disputes Redressal Commission has addressed this issue, deciding in favour of the landowners.
What the case is about
The dispute originated in 2010, when two landowners, along with their late mother, transferred their development rights to a builder for redevelopment. They held a one-third undivided share in a property in Mumbai, and executed an Agreement to Assign for the redevelopment.
Subsequently, they also entered into a Supplementary Agreement dated February 18, 2015, and an Agreement to Offer Permanent Alternate Accommodation (PAA), executed on the same date.
In their complaint before the Consumer Commission, the landowners said that the builder had agreed to allot them a 1,395 sq. ft. flat in the newly constructed building, along with two car parking spaces.
The agreement also required the developer to pay monetary compensation, rent for temporary alternative accommodation and a penalty if possession was delayed.
In addition, the builder was responsible for executing and registering the agreement and bearing the stamp duty and registration charges for up to 1,000 sq. ft. of the allotted area.
The landowners received physical possession of the flat in May 2018. However, according to an ET report quoting their complaint, the developer neither paid its agreed share of the stamp duty nor executed the registered PAA Agreement.
They also alleged that the builder had not paid the enhanced compensation of Rs 88 lakh for the increased floor space index (FSI), as stipulated in the Supplementary Agreement.
Other outstanding amounts included Rs 6,60,000 towards rent for temporary accommodation for the period from December 2017 to April 2018, Rs 16,50,000 as a penalty for delayed possession, and Rs 10,00,000 to reimburse the cost of raw materials they had purchased.
Instead of meeting these commitments, the landowners claimed, the developer sent them a “baseless legal notice” in June 2022, demanding Rs 30,26,592 towards alleged construction expenses.
Why did the Consumer Commission rule in favour of the landowners?
Legal experts point out that the landowners were able to establish their entitlements because these had been explicitly documented in agreements executed between the parties.
The developer's failure to honour contractual commitments that were clearly set out in these documents was another important factor in the outcome, Bhargav KS, Managing Partner at K.S & B.K.S Law Associates, Bengaluru, told ET.
The agreements specified the landowners' rights to alternative accommodation, enhanced FSI compensation, rent during the transit period, compensation for delayed possession and registration. Their affidavits and correspondence provided evidence of the developer's defaults, while the fact that possession was handed over only in May 2018 helped establish the delay in delivery.
The Commission also recognised that surrendering development rights amounted to consideration for “housing services”.
The Commission noted that the developer had obtained the benefits of the development rights and handed over possession of the flat in May 2018, but had failed to complete a key statutory requirement.
The Commission reportedly said, "the developer blatantly ignored the statutory mandate of the Maharashtra Ownership Flats Act, 1963, by failing to register the Agreement to Offer Permanent Alternate Accommodation,".
It also found that the builder had withheld financial benefits legitimately due to the landowners. The Commission observed that the demand notices seeking Rs 30,26,592 from the landowners amounted to a clear instance of an unfair trade practice.
According to the Commission, the developer's actions reflected a serious and deliberate failure to discharge both its contractual commitments and statutory responsibilities.
The matter was heard ex parte against the developer, which did not appear despite receiving notice.
The Commission consequently directed the builder to execute and register the Agreement to Offer Permanent Alternate Accommodation within 60 days of receiving the order. It also instructed the developer to bear the stamp duty and registration charges for up to 1,000 sq. ft. of carpet area.
The builder was further ordered to pay Rs 88 lakh as compensation for enhanced FSI, with interest at 8% from the date of default until the amount is actually recovered by the landowners. The directions also included payment of Rs 6,60,000 towards outstanding rent for temporary accommodation and Rs 16,50,000 as a penalty for delayed possession, the ET report said.
In addition, the developer must reimburse Rs 10,00,000 for the raw materials purchased by the landowners. The Commission awarded a further Rs 1,00,000 as compensation for mental agony, harassment and hardship, along with Rs 50,000 towards litigation expenses.
Taken together, the directions require the builder to pay the landowners more than Rs 1.22 crore, besides complying with the order to execute and register the permanent alternate accommodation agreement.

briefs.headline: NTPC leads second round of coal gasification bids with two applications
briefs.deck: The third round of the rolling window for coal gasification projects also opened Tuesday, November 10.
briefs.bodyText:
Two applications, both from state-owned power producer NTPC Ltd, have been received in the second rolling round of applications for incentives to set up coal gasification projects, the Coal Ministry said on Tuesday. The ministry also announced the launch of the third round under the government’s ₹37,500-crore incentive scheme.
NTPC has sought incentives for projects to produce urea, methanol and dimethyl ether (DME). In the first round, it had applied for incentives to set up a synthetic natural gas production project.
A total of seven applications were received in the first round, including three from Adani Enterprises for urea production projects. The remaining applications covered projects involving synthetic natural gas and direct reduced iron, among other products.
Commenting on the response, Atanu Mukherjee, Chief Executive Officer of energy engineering and advisory firm Dastur Energy, said, “NTPC’s continued participation is encouraging. However, the limited response in the second round highlights the need to complement financial incentives with schemes that help create commercially viable and bankable coal gasification projects that attract wider private-sector investment.”
He said the government’s ₹37,500-crore scheme provides a strong foundation, but viability-gap funding alone may not be sufficient.
“Even commercially sound projects can struggle to secure financing because lenders remain cautious about technology, construction and operating risks, particularly where domestic commercial precedents are limited,” he said.
The Coal Ministry said successive rolling rounds were aimed at widening industry participation, attracting investments and accelerating the adoption of coal gasification technologies.
India has set a target of gasifying 100 million tonnes of coal by 2030.
